claims.text: Grants are available for conservation, restoration, interpretation, and education spaces for historic buildings and landscapes of national significance.
The funding is for organizations managing sites of outstanding historic, architectural, and cultural significance with a clear emphasis on public access and engagement.
Eligible organizations must be registered charities or local authorities.
The site must be open and accessible to the public for the majority of the year with a reasonable number of visitors.
The site must be listed as Grade I, II* or a Scheduled Monument (England and Wales), Category A, B or a Scheduled Monument (Scotland), or Grade A, B+ or a Scheduled Monument (Northern Ireland).
Projects should involve restoration or conservation work to the historic fabric of the building, or excellent interpretation of historic buildings, landscapes, and collections.

Projects should aim to increase visitor numbers, improve public engagement with and understanding of sites of historical and cultural significance, or improve the future sustainability of the organization.

For landscapes, parks, and gardens, there must be a case for national significance, and the project should involve conservation or restoration of built heritage or interpretation of built heritage or past human existence.
Projects primarily related to the conservation and interpretation of natural heritage are unlikely to be eligible.
The application process is two-stage.
Stage 1 applications are submitted online and require a brief project description, total cost, funding shortfall, proposed timetable, and confirmation of institutional support.
Audited accounts for the past two years are required for Stage 1 applications.
Stage 2 applications are by invitation only.
At least 25% of capital costs must be raised before submitting a Stage 2 application, unless the project cost is under £50,000.
Necessary planning permission should be in place for Stage 2 applications.
Organizations that have previously received a grant must wait five years before applying again for a different project, unless they are universities or large charities with multiple sites.
Organizations turned down at Stage 1 can submit a new application for a different project at any time.
Organizations turned down at Stage 2 must wait at least one year before submitting a new application for a different project.
The same project will not normally be considered twice.
There are two funding rounds per year.
For Round 1, Stage 1 applications are open from November 20th and the deadline is January 5th.
For Round 1, Stage 2 applications have a deadline of March 1st.
For Round 2, Stage 1 applications are open from May 14th and the deadline is July 1st.
For Round 2, Stage 2 applications have a deadline of September 1st.
Funding decisions are made in June for Round 1 and December for Round 2.
If a deadline falls on a weekend, applications received by 9 am on the following Monday are accepted.
Grants are not made retrospectively; projects must be ongoing at the time of the funding decision.
An invitation to Stage 2 remains open for three funding rounds unless otherwise agreed.
The minimum grant amount is £15,000.
The usual grant range is £15,000 – £100,000.
Match funding is required if the project cost is over £50,000.
The funding programme is for Heritage, Humanities & the Arts.
